source.title: Entry and Exit Confessions of a Champion Trader — 52 Ways a Professional Speculator Gets In and Out of the Stock, Futures and Forex Markets
source.author: Kevin J. Davey
source.bonus_eld_files: http://www.AOKbooks.com/52book (all entries/exits as TradeStation ELD files)
notes: tradestation_code is the book's EasyLanguage verbatim, with PDF line-wrap artifacts repaired (e.g. '9 35' -> '935', 'AdxT hresh' -> 'AdxThresh'). Nothing was corrected semantically — where the code looks wrong or contradicts the plain-English text, that is recorded in `discrepancies`, and the CODE is what the book's ELD files run.

parameters lists every Var/Input the book declares with its default. Bare literals that are clearly tunable (e.g. adx(15) < 20) are listed under `hardcoded_constants` so they can become inputs when the rule is authored.

composite: true means the rule is several independently meaningful conditions ANDed at the top level, which /author-rule would split. `decomposition` maps each piece to an existing rule in rules/CATALOG.md where one exists, or names a new rule. Per Brian's plan the decomposed atomic rules will be created AND the exact composite will be kept as its own rule for testing against the book.

el_words_unregistered lists EasyLanguage words the rule needs that have NO row in rules/EL_FEATURES.md. /author-rule §4 blocks a rule on any such word until a probe measures it; several words recur across many rules, so one probe can unblock a whole group (see `blocking_features_summary`).

order_type records how the book places the order. The corpus today emits condition-based rules that fill at the next bar's open ('next bar at market'); 'stop at price' / 'limit at price' entries and exits need generator/engine support before they can be mirrored (see `plan_considerations`).
The book's plain English for each rule is paraphrased in `description`; the 'General Concept' rationale is condensed into `rationale`.

plan_considerations: ORDER TYPES: 17 of the 43 entries and 2 of the exits place STOP or LIMIT orders at a computed price (breakouts at highest high, close +/- k*ATR, prior-day high/low, limit at close). The corpus only has 'condition true at bar close -> fill at next open'. Reproducing these exactly needs a stop/limit entry-order path in the generator and engine (with EL's fill semantics for a stop/limit inside the next bar). This is the biggest structural gap and should be settled before authoring those rules.

PRICE-LEVEL EXITS: Exit #2 uses SetStopLoss/SetProfitTarget (intrabar, dollar-based, per contract) and Exit #10 uses limit/stop exit orders at price. The corpus's StopLoss/TakeProfit evaluate OpenPositionProfit at bar close and exit next bar at market — different behaviour, not a parameter difference. Exit #2 method 1 is therefore NOT StopLoss + TakeProfit as they exist today.

UNREGISTERED EL WORDS: Percentile, Stochastic, MoneyFlow, CCI, UltimateOsc, XAverage, TriAverage, BollingerBand, CountIF, EntriesToday, HighD/LowD/OpenD/CloseD, PositionProfit(n), TotalTrades, Year, 'crosses above/below/over/under', and time[1]/date[1] history all lack rows in EL_FEATURES.md. Each needs a probe (or a deliberate ACCEPTED row) before /author-rule will save a rule using it. Grouping the probes by word rather than by rule will save a lot of TradeStation time.

INTRADAY-ONLY RULES: Entries #7, #8, #9, #10, #18, #20, #40 and Exit #7 depend on Time / daily-bar reference functions and only make sense on intraday bars. Whether the test universe includes intraday bars determines whether they are worth authoring first.

WFSafe DECISION: the book calls plain ADX / RSI / AvgTrueRange. The 2026-08-25 decision for the AI-Algos book was to use the WFSafe_ variants everywhere (ADX and RSI are measured identical at fixed length; ATR is the rolling form). Assume the same here unless Brian says otherwise.
EQUALITY: every 'close = highest(close, n)' in the book becomes '>=' in C++ (the `=` trap, Breakout.json). Listed once here rather than per rule.
Nothing else in the extract suggests changing the plan: extract -> author atomic rules -> author exact composites -> test composites against the book.

rules.name: Go With The Flow
rules.rationale: Trade in the direction of 1-bar momentum; as soon as a bar closes with the open position showing a loss beyond a threshold, reverse. Author used it in metals.
rules.description: If close < previous close AND (open position profit < -openloss OR flat), sell short next bar at market. If close > previous close AND (open position profit < -openloss OR flat), buy next bar at market.

decomposition.maps_to: Momentum (existing), lookback=1
NEW entry filter, e.g. FlatOrOpenLossExceeds(openloss) — same both sides; note the OR is not splittable across panes, so this stays one rule

notes: An Entry that reads OpenPositionProfit — the author-rule role check would flag it, but it is genuinely an entry filter (it decides whether a new signal may reverse the open position).
Because the entry is also the reversal, this is a stop-and-reverse system with an implicit loss exit; no separate exit is needed but one can be added.
openloss is dollars per contract; OpenPositionProfit is net of entry-side costs (EL_FEATURES.md).

rules.name: Everyone Loves Friday
rules.rationale: Once-a-week entry: if Friday's close is the highest close of the lookback, go long at the next bar (Monday/Sunday-night open). Written for daily bars. Author used it in energies.
rules.description: If the bar's day of week is Friday (5) AND close is the highest close of the last bbars bars, buy next bar at market. If Friday AND close is the lowest close of the last bbars bars, sell short next bar at market.

decomposition.maps_to: DayOfWeekEntry (existing), dayLong=5, dayShort=5
Breakout (existing), lookback=bbars

notes: Fully covered by existing rules; the composite is DayOfWeekEntry(5,5) AND Breakout(25).
On intraday bars the signal would need restricting to the last bar of the day (author's note).

rules.name: Books Can Be Great
rules.rationale: Countertrend moving-average cross adapted from Tushar Chande's 'Beyond Technical Analysis' (long-only there, made bidirectional). Author used it in stocks and stock indices.
rules.description: If the shortma-bar average of close crosses BELOW the longma-bar average AND close < short average, buy next bar at market. If the short average crosses ABOVE the long average AND close > short average, sell short next bar at market.

decomposition.maps_to: NEW MovingAverageCross(fastLength, slowLength) — a crossing, never split; long side = fast crosses ABOVE slow, so E3's long uses it FLIPPED (E13 uses it un-flipped)
CloseAboveAverage (existing), lookback=shortma, FLIPPED

notes: 'crosses below' in EL is true on the bar where A < B and A[1] >= B[1] (needs a register row to confirm the tie handling).
Note the shortma input is shared by the cross and the filter — decomposing into two rules gives each its own length.

rules.name: Breakout With A Twist
rules.rationale: Breakouts mostly fail; take them only when ADX says the market is NOT trending, on the idea that breakouts out of flat periods lead to bigger trends. Author used it in metals.
rules.description: If the 15-bar ADX < 20, buy next bar on a stop at the highest high of the last len bars, and sell short next bar on a stop at the lowest low of the last len bars.
rules.order_type: stop at price (highest high / lowest low of len bars, including current bar)

decomposition.maps_to: AdxBelowThreshold (existing), lookback=15, threshold=20

decomposition.piece: buy next bar at highest(high,len) stop
decomposition.maps_to: NEW stop-entry rule, e.g. HighestHighStopEntry(len) — requires stop-order entry support

notes: Both orders are placed every bar the filter passes, so this is stop-and-reverse.
ADX: use WFSafe_ADX per the 2026-08-25 decision (measured identical at fixed length).

rules.name: Average True Range Based Breakout
rules.rationale: A breakout must be large relative to recent volatility to count: the next bar has to move XX ATRs beyond the current close. Author used it in grains/agriculturals.
rules.description: Buy next bar on a stop at close + XX * AvgTrueRange(ATRval). Sell short next bar on a stop at close - XX * AvgTrueRange(ATRval).

decomposition.maps_to: NEW AtrRangeStopEntry(atrLookback, multiple) — requires stop-order entry support; ATR = WFSafe_AvgTrueRange rolling form (AtrProfitTarget reference)

notes: No condition at all — orders are live every bar; stop-and-reverse.
Compare E34, which is the countertrend cousin using Average(TrueRange,3) over a variable rather than AvgTrueRange.

rules.name: Percent Ranker
rules.rationale: Low prices lead to lower prices and high to higher: sell when the close is in the lower quartile of recent closes, buy in the upper quartile — but only while ADX shows a moderate trend (20–30), to avoid flat ranges.
rules.description: Value1 = 25th percentile of the last xbars closes; Value2 = 75th percentile. If 20 < ADX(14) < 30 AND close < Value1, sell short next bar at market. If 20 < ADX(14) < 30 AND close > Value2, buy next bar at market.

decomposition.maps_to: AdxBelowThreshold (existing), threshold=20, NEGATED
AdxBelowThreshold (existing), threshold=30

decomposition.piece: close > percentile(.75, close, xbars) (long) / close < percentile(.25, ...) (short)
decomposition.maps_to: NEW ClosePercentileValue(percentile, lookback) — EL's Percentile() interpolates a VALUE; the existing ClosePercentileRank ranks the close itself and is a different calculation

notes: Percentile(pct, series, length) is an EL function whose interpolation method must be probed (shared with X5).
Negating '< 20' gives '>= 20', the book has '> 20' — indistinguishable in practice for a double-valued ADX but worth noting for the exact composite.

rules.name: Intraday Breakout
rules.rationale: Short-term breakout of the prior day's high/low, only inside a chosen time-of-day window, at most one entry per day, and only when ADX shows a trend. Intraday bars only.
rules.description: If bar time is within [tbeg, tend] AND there have been no entries today AND ADX(adxP) >= adxThresh, buy next bar on a stop at yesterday's high + offset and sell short next bar on a stop at yesterday's low - offset.
rules.order_type: stop at price (prior day high/low +/- offset points)

decomposition.maps_to: NEW TimeWindow(start, end) entry filter — same both sides
NEW MaxEntriesPerDay(n) filter — needs a ctx built-in or EL probe
AdxBelowThreshold (existing) NEGATED (gives >=, matching the book exactly here)

decomposition.piece: stop at highd(1) + offset / lowd(1) - offset
decomposition.maps_to: NEW PriorDayHighLowStopEntry(offset) — requires stop-order entry support and HighD/LowD

notes: offset is in price points, so its useful value is instrument-specific.
Intraday only.

rules.name: Intraday Breakout With Expanding Range
rules.rationale: E7 plus a range-expansion condition: yesterday's range must exceed the range of two days ago, on the idea that expansion continues.
rules.description: As E7, with the additional condition that (yesterday's high - low) > (high - low of two days ago).
rules.order_type: stop at price (prior day high/low +/- offset points)

decomposition.maps_to: see E7
NEW DailyRangeExpanding filter — same both sides; E41's filter is exactly this NEGATED (range contracting), so one rule serves both

notes: Intraday only.

rules.name: Day Of Week Trading
rules.rationale: Exploit a day-of-week bias with a reason behind it (e.g. the Wednesday EIA energy report). Uses time of day as a trigger, so minute bars are required; the order is valid for one bar only.
rules.description: At the 9:35 bar on Wednesday (3), buy next bar on a stop at yesterday's high. At the 9:35 bar on Thursday (4), sell short next bar on a stop at yesterday's low.
rules.tradestation_code:
If time=935 and dayofweek(date)=3 then Buy next bar at highd(1) stop;
If time=935 and dayofweek(date)=4 then SellShort next bar at lowd(1) stop;
rules.order_type: stop at price (prior day high / low)

decomposition.maps_to: NEW TimeOfDayEquals(time) filter — same both sides
DayOfWeekEntry (existing), dayLong=3, dayShort=4
NEW PriorDayHighLowStopEntry(offset=0) — shared with E7/E8/E10/E11

notes: Author warns trades are infrequent: one bar of validity and price must already be near yesterday's extreme.
Intraday only (remove the time test for daily bars).

rules.name: Enhanced Day Of Week Trading
rules.rationale: E9 with a momentum confirmation added — shown to illustrate adding conditions to an entry.
rules.description: As E9, plus close > close[xbars] for the long and close < close[xbars] for the short.
rules.order_type: stop at price (prior day high / low)

decomposition.maps_to: see E9
Momentum (existing), lookback=xbars

notes: Intraday only.

rules.name: NOT Day Of Week Trading
rules.rationale: The inverse of E9: exclude one day of the week instead of selecting one.
rules.description: On every day except Wednesday (3), buy next bar on a stop at yesterday's high. On every day except Thursday (4), sell short next bar on a stop at yesterday's low.
rules.tradestation_code:
If dayofweek(date)<> 3 then Buy next bar at highd(1) stop;
If dayofweek(date)<> 4 then SellShort next bar at lowd(1) stop;
rules.order_type: stop at price (prior day high / low)

decomposition.maps_to: DayOfWeekEntry (existing), dayLong=3, dayShort=4, NEGATED
NEW PriorDayHighLowStopEntry(offset=0)

notes: No time test, so it works on daily bars too (where highd(1) is simply high[1]).

rules.name: RSI Trigger
rules.rationale: Classic RSI overbought/oversold, combined with a close-above-average trend check. Author used it with stocks, ETFs, stock indices.
rules.description: If RSI(close, RSILength) < RSIThreshold AND close > Average(close, XBars), buy next bar at market. If RSI > 100 - RSIThreshold AND close < Average(close, XBars), sell short next bar at market.

decomposition.maps_to: RsiBelowThreshold (existing), lookback=5, threshold=80 — exact match including the 100-T short side
CloseAboveAverage (existing), lookback=5

notes: Fully covered by existing rules: RsiBelowThreshold(5,80) AND CloseAboveAverage(5).
RSI = WFSafe_RSI per the standing decision (identical to plain RSI at fixed length).

rules.name: Moving Average Cross, With A Twist
rules.rationale: The standard MA crossover, but only if the close has not run away from the previous bar's low/high — filters crosses caused by price spikes. Author used it in softs and agriculturals.
rules.description: If Average(close, FastLength) crosses above Average(close, SlowLength) AND close < low[1] + XX, buy next bar at market. If the fast average crosses below the slow average AND close > high[1] - XX, sell short next bar at market.

decomposition.piece: fast average crosses above slow average
decomposition.maps_to: NEW MovingAverageCross(fastLength, slowLength) — shared with E3 (E3 uses it flipped)

decomposition.piece: close < low[1] + XX (long) / close > high[1] - XX (short)
decomposition.maps_to: NEW CloseNearPriorLow(threshold) — threshold in price points (instrument-specific; a tick- or ATR-based variant may be worth adding but is not the book's rule)

rules.name: Split Week, Part 1
rules.rationale: Mid-week (Tue/Wed/Thu) behaves differently from days adjacent to the weekend. Enter on a joint highest-high and highest-close, filtered to low-volatility conditions via ATR in dollars. Author used it in metals and currencies.
rules.description: If the day is Tuesday, Wednesday or Thursday AND high = highest high of bbars AND close = highest close of bbars AND AvgTrueRange(14) * BigPointValue < maxl, buy next bar at market. Mirror (lowest low, lowest close) for the short.

decomposition.maps_to: NEW DayOfWeekRange(firstDay, lastDay) or DayOfWeekSet filter — DayOfWeekEntry takes one day per side and panes AND, so an OR of days needs its own rule
NEW HighestHighBreakout(lookback) — high >= highest high of N bars (Breakout is on closes)
Breakout (existing), lookback=bbars
NEW AtrDollarsBelow(atrLookback, maxDollars) filter — same both sides; BigPointValue is unconverted (EL_FEATURES.md)

notes: Shares the whole body with E15; only the day set differs.

rules.name: Split Week, Part 2
rules.rationale: The weekend-adjacent half of E14: signals only on Friday and Monday.
rules.description: As E14, but the day must be Friday (5) or Monday (1).

decomposition.maps_to: same day-set rule as E14 (NOT a contiguous range — a set, or the negation of E14's {2,3,4} on a Mon–Fri market)
see E14

notes: On a Monday–Friday market, {5,1} is exactly NOT {2,3,4}, so E14's day filter negated reproduces it — unless Sunday-night bars exist (dayofweek 0), which fall in neither set.

rules.name: Introducing Serial Correlation
rules.rationale: Make the next trade depend on the last: wait 5 bars after a winner, 20 after a loser, before taking a new countertrend signal (buy the lowest close, sell the highest).
rules.description: If (last position was profitable AND >= 5 bars since its exit) OR (last position lost AND >= 20 bars since exit) OR no trades yet: buy next bar at market if close = lowest close of xbars; sell short if close = highest close of xbars.

decomposition.maps_to: Breakout (existing), lookback=xbars, FLIPPED
NEW LastTradeCooldown(waitAfterWin, waitAfterLoss) filter — same both sides; the OR of three terms is one rule

notes: BarsSinceExit(1) IS registered (VERIFIED, wants an index). PositionProfit(1) and TotalTrades are not.
Signal-time gate while a position may be open: the book's EL evaluates it on every bar regardless of MarketPosition, so it also gates reversals.

rules.name: Back In Style
rules.rationale: A 4-bar price pattern modified from Michael Harris ('Profitability and Systematic Trading'). Worked in stocks early 2000s, faltered 2011–2017, came back 2018.
rules.description: Short: low[3] > high AND high > low[1] AND low > low[2] AND low[1] > low[2] — sell short next bar at open. Long: high[3] < low AND low < high[1] AND high < high[2] AND high[1] < high[2] — buy next bar at open.
rules.tradestation_code:
if (l[3] > h[0] AND h[0] > l[1] AND l[0] > l[2] AND l[1] > l[2]) then sellshort Next Bar at open;

if (h[3] < l[0] AND l[0] < h[1] AND h[0] < h[2] AND h[1] < h[2]) then buy Next Bar at open;
rules.order_type: market next bar ('next bar at open')

decomposition.maps_to: NEW HarrisGapPattern (name TBD) — a single 4-bar pattern; the comparisons are not independently meaningful

notes: Reaches back 3 bars.
E30 is the first three terms of this pattern with the sides swapped plus a momentum term.

rules.name: Where You At?
rules.rationale: A 2-bar stochastic: where the close sits in the range of the last two bars. Mean-reverting — sell strength, buy weakness. Ignores signals in the early night session (24-hour futures). Author used it in stocks and stock indices.
rules.description: If time < 1600 or time > 2300: ll = min(low, low[1]); hh = max(high, high[1]). If (close - ll) / (hh - ll + 0.000001) >= thresh, sell short next bar at market. If it is <= 1 - thresh, buy next bar at market.

decomposition.maps_to: NEW TimeWindow filter NEGATED (window 1600–2300 excluded) — shares the rule with E7
NEW TwoBarRangePosition(threshold) — mean-reversion form; note E38/E39 use the single-bar (c-l)/(h-l) version

notes: At thresh = 0.5 both conditions can be true on the same bar (value exactly 0.5) — TS then queues both; exits-before-entries and max_entries semantics decide the outcome.
minlist/maxlist are UNKNOWN for tolerance but here compare tick-grid prices, so inert (CLAUDE.md).
The epsilon changes the low bits of the ratio; must be reproduced literally.

rules.name: Exponentially Better
rules.rationale: Dual exponential-moving-average crossover, slow length fixed at 4x the fast, entering on a stop at the signal bar's high/low. Originally used in metals.
rules.description: avg1 = XAverage(close, lookbackdays); avg2 = XAverage(close, 4 * lookbackdays). If avg1 > avg2 AND avg1[1] < avg2[1], buy next bar on a stop at this bar's high. If avg1 < avg2 AND avg1[1] > avg2[1], sell short next bar on a stop at this bar's low.
rules.order_type: stop at price (current bar high / low)

decomposition.maps_to: NEW EmaCross(fastLength, slowMultiple) — a crossing (keep whole); STRICT on the prior bar (an exact tie last bar does not count), unlike EL's 'crosses above'

decomposition.piece: buy next bar at high stop
decomposition.maps_to: NEW CurrentBarHighLowStopEntry — requires stop-order entry support

discrepancies: avg1(10) and avg2(20) initial values are overwritten every bar; the comment 'lengths' on lookbackdays is the only real parameter.
notes: XAverage's seed and warm-up behaviour (and MW's WFSafe_XAverage, if one exists) must be probed; avg1[1] reads a variable's history so bar-1 reads 0.

rules.name: Range Breakout
rules.rationale: Daily-range breakout on intraday bars: at the first bar of each calendar day capture the open and the prior day's true range, average the last 10 daily ranges, then buy/sell on stops at today's open +/- a fraction of that average, before 13:00.
rules.description: On the first bar of a new calendar date: todayopen = open; shift the 10-slot range history; range01 = max(|dayhigh - close two days ago|, |daylow - close two days ago|, dayhigh - daylow) using the previous day's tracked high/low; reset dayhigh/daylow. Every bar: rangeavg = mean of the 10 stored ranges; track dayhigh/daylow. If time < 1300: buy next bar on a stop at todayopen + xfl * rangeavg; sell short next bar on a stop at todayopen - xfs * rangeavg.
rules.order_type: stop at price (today's open +/- fraction of 10-day average range)

decomposition.maps_to: NEW TimeBefore(cutoff) filter (or TimeWindow with start 0) — same both sides

decomposition.piece: stateful daily-range tracking + stop at todayopen +/- k*rangeavg
decomposition.maps_to: NEW DailyRangeStopEntry(longFraction, shortFraction, rangeDays=10) — stateful preConditionHook; requires stop-order entry support

discrepancies: range01 uses yesterdayclose02 (the close TWO days ago, as the variable is assigned before use in the same block) against yesterday's high/low — not the close preceding yesterday's session. Reproduce as written.

yesterdayclose01 = close[1] on the first bar of the day is the last bar of the previous day — correct, but the shift makes yesterdayclose02 the day-before-yesterday's last close only from the second day on.
notes: New day is by calendar date (date <> date[1]), not session — EL Date is the wall-clock close date (VERIFIED).
Warm-up: all range slots are 0 for the first 10 days, so rangeavg ramps up; the first day's range01 uses the sentinel dayhigh/daylow. Zero-fill exactly as EL variables do.
The sum for rangeavg is written left-to-right over 10 terms; keep the operand order.
maxlist over price differences (tick grid) — inert tolerance question.
Intraday only.

rules.name: Asymmetric Triple
rules.rationale: An asymmetric entry the author dislikes but that worked (on a foreign stock index): long on a stop above the close, short on a stop below today's low; the long is additionally filtered by a triple average of daily lows versus a lagged low.
rules.description: EntryL = close + ATRmult * AvgTrueRange(14); EntryS = LowD(0) - ATRmult * AvgTrueRange(14). Long is allowed only if TriAverage(LowD(0), Length1) >= low[Length2]; short is always allowed. Buy next bar at EntryL stop; sell short next bar at EntryS stop.
rules.order_type: stop at price (asymmetric: close + k*ATR long, LowD(0) - k*ATR short)

decomposition.maps_to: NEW TriAverageDailyLowFilter(length1, length2) — long side only; short side always true
NEW AsymmetricAtrStopEntry — requires stop-order entry support; the long anchor is the bar close, the short anchor is today's session low

discrepancies: ATRmult defaults to 0 in the book, which makes the ATR term vanish (EntryL = close, EntryS = LowD(0)). Presumably meant to be optimized; keep 0 as the printed default.
notes: Rules built for a stock index with an upward bias; the author cautions against asymmetric rules elsewhere.

rules.name: Asymmetric Again
rules.rationale: Another asymmetric entry: long only on a gap-up day (today's open >= yesterday's close), on a stop above the open; short always, on a stop below today's low.
rules.description: EntryL = OpenD(0) + ATRmult * AvgTrueRange(14); EntryS = LowD(0) - ATRmult * AvgTrueRange(14). Long allowed only if OpenD(0) >= CloseD(1); short always. Buy next bar at EntryL stop; sell short next bar at EntryS stop.
rules.order_type: stop at price (asymmetric: OpenD(0) + k*ATR long, LowD(0) - k*ATR short)

decomposition.maps_to: NEW GapUpFilter — long side only; short side always true
NEW AsymmetricAtrStopEntry variant anchored on OpenD(0) / LowD(0)

discrepancies: Plain English says 'open is greater than yesterday's close'; code is >=.

rules.name: Stochastic Cross
rules.rationale: Use the stochastic %K / %D cross on its own as a signal rather than as a confirmation filter.
rules.description: Compute the Stochastic with SLength, Smoothing1, Smoothing2, SmoothingType. If SlowK crosses over SlowD, buy next bar at market. If SlowK crosses under SlowD, sell short next bar at market.

decomposition.maps_to: NEW StochasticCross(length, smoothing1, smoothing2, smoothingType) — a crossing

notes: The Stochastic function's exact formulation (SmoothingType 1 = simple, 2 = exponential per TS docs) and MW's WFSafe variant, if any, need a probe.

rules.name: Show Me The Money (Flow)
rules.rationale: Money Flow Index (0–100, volume-weighted RSI-like) leaving oversold = buy; leaving overbought = sell.
rules.description: MoneyFlowVal = MoneyFlow(Length). If it crosses above OverSold, buy next bar at market. If it crosses below Overbought, sell short next bar at market.
rules.sides: mirrored when Overbought = 100 - OverSold (separate inputs in the book)

decomposition.maps_to: NEW MoneyFlowCross(length, oversold, overbought) — a crossing

notes: MoneyFlow uses Volume — recall EL Volume on TS futures charts is up-ticks (EL_FEATURES.md); the probe must establish which series the function reads.
MoneyFlowVal is a variable: its history is zero-filled during warm-up, which matters for the 'crosses' test on the first calculated bar.

rules.name: Classic Bollinger Bands
rules.rationale: Bollinger Band re-entry (close crossing back over the lower band) confirmed by simple momentum, entered at market.
rules.description: LowerBand = BollingerBand(close, Length, -NumDevs); UpperBand = BollingerBand(close, Length, +NumDevs). If close crosses over LowerBand AND close > close[Length2], buy next bar at market. If close crosses under UpperBand AND close < close[Length2], sell short next bar at market.

decomposition.piece: close crosses over lower band (long) / under upper band (short)
decomposition.maps_to: NEW BollingerBandCross(length, numDevs) — a crossing; population StdDev (VERIFIED)
Momentum (existing), lookback=Length2

discrepancies: The plain-English text omits the momentum condition that the code has.
notes: LowerBand/UpperBand are variables (zero history in warm-up) — affects the 'crosses' comparison on the first calculated bar.

rules.name: Classic Keltner Channel
rules.rationale: Same idea as E25 with a Keltner channel (average +/- k * ATR) instead of Bollinger Bands.
rules.description: LowerBand = Average(close, Length) - NumATRs * AvgTrueRange(Length); UpperBand = Average(close, Length) + NumATRs * AvgTrueRange(Length). If close crosses over LowerBand AND close > close[Length2], buy next bar at market. If close crosses under UpperBand AND close < close[Length2], sell short next bar at market.

decomposition.piece: close crosses over lower Keltner band / under upper
decomposition.maps_to: NEW KeltnerChannelCross(length, numAtrs) — a crossing; ATR = WFSafe_AvgTrueRange rolling form, same length as the average
Momentum (existing), lookback=Length2

discrepancies: Plain-English text omits the momentum condition.
notes: Band variables are zero-filled in warm-up, as E25.

rules.name: Three Amigos
rules.rationale: A composite of ADX trend filter, RSI below/above midline, and opposing long- and short-term momentum (a pullback within a trend). Author used it in currencies and metals; warns against optimizing all parameters.
rules.description: If ADX(ADXLength) > 25: buy next bar at market if RSI(close, RSILength) < 50 AND close < close[lookbackBig] AND close > close[lookbackshort]; sell short if RSI > 50 AND close > close[lookbackBig] AND close < close[lookbackshort].

decomposition.maps_to: AdxBelowThreshold (existing), lookback=14, threshold=25, NEGATED (>= 25 vs book's > 25)
RsiBelowThreshold (existing), lookback=14, threshold=50 — short side 100-50 = 50, exact
Momentum (existing), lookback=20, FLIPPED
Momentum (existing), lookback=10

rules.name: Pitter Patter Pattern
rules.rationale: A simplified, bidirectional 2-bar pattern based on Michael Harris' work. Author uses it on daily Unleaded Gas.
rules.description: Long: open[1] > high AND open > close[1] AND close[1] > low[1] AND low[1] > close — buy next bar at market. Short: open[1] < low AND open < close[1] AND close[1] < high[1] AND high[1] < close — sell short next bar at market.

If o[1] > h[0] AND o[0] > c[1] AND c[1] > l[1] AND l[1] > c[0] then buy next bar at market;

if  o[1] < l[0] AND o[0] < c[1] AND c[1] < h[1] AND h[1] < c[0] then sell short next bar at market;

rules.name: Quick Pullback Pattern

rules.name: Breakdown Dead Ahead
rules.rationale: Countertrend stop entry: when momentum is up, place a sell-short stop a multiple of recent true range below the close (and vice versa) — a move that far against the trend suggests a breakdown. Author used it in softs.
rules.description: myrange = TrueRange. If close > close[momen], sell short next bar on a stop at close - mult * Average(myrange, 3). If close < close[momen], buy next bar on a stop at close + mult * Average(myrange, 3).

rules.name: Commodity Channel Index
rules.rationale: CCI, smoothed, used alone as a countertrend signal at +/-100. Author used it in currencies.

rules.name: Big Tail Bars
rules.rationale: Count 'bull tail' bars (up close, lower wick longer than the body, higher high) and 'bear tail' bars over a window; enter long when bull tails dominate and exceed a threshold.
rules.description: BullBarTail = count over Period bars of (close > open AND open - low > close - open AND high > high[1]). BearBarTail = count of (close < open AND high - open > open - close AND low < low[1]). If BullBarTail > BearBarTail AND BullBarTail > thresh, buy next bar at market. If BullBarTail < BearBarTail AND BearBarTail > thresh, sell short next bar at market.

Open - Low > Close - Open is a comparison of price differences — tick grid, tolerance inert.

rules.name: New High With Consecutive Highs
rules.rationale: A close above the prior N-bar highest high, confirmed by short-term momentum (two consecutive up closes and above the close 3 bars ago). Author used it in currencies and metals; suggests the reverse for stock indices.
rules.description: Long: close > Highest(high, xbars)[1] AND close > close[1] AND close > close[3] AND close[1] > close[2] — buy next bar at market. Short: mirror with Lowest(low, xbars)[1] and reversed comparisons.

rules.name: Start With an Awesome Oscillator
rules.rationale: Bill Williams' Awesome Oscillator (difference of two averages of the bar midpoint), used as a divergence signal against a lower-low / higher-high bar with a strong close in the opposite direction.
rules.description: AO = Average((H+L)/2, v1) - Average((H+L)/2, v1+v3). Condition1 = AO[aback] > AO[bback]; Condition2 = AO[aback] < AO[bback]. Condition3 = low < low[1] AND (close-low)/(high-low+0.000001) > fatr. Condition4 = high > high[1] AND (close-low)/(high-low+0.000001) < 1-fatr. If Condition1 AND Condition4, sell short next bar at market. If Condition2 AND Condition3, buy next bar at market.

rules.rationale: Seasonal restriction: January–June long only, July–December short only, combined with a highest/lowest close and a close-position-in-bar term. Author uses it for Soybeans.
rules.description: If month <= 6 AND close = highest close of xbar bars AND (close-low)/(high-low) < thresh, buy next bar at market. If month > 6 AND close = lowest close of xbar bars AND (close-low)/(high-low) > 1-thresh, sell short next bar at market.

rules.name: It's About Time!
rules.rationale: Time-of-day bias: certain times of day favour buying (just after 03:00 and 21:30) and others selling (after 09:00), confirmed by momentum, entered on a limit at the current close. Developed for Bitcoin futures (XBT), 2017–18.
rules.description: As CODED: BullSignalTime latches true the first time the bar time crosses 03:00 or 21:30; BearSignalTime latches true the first time it crosses 09:00 — neither is ever reset. Once latched, buy next bar on a limit at the close whenever close > close[barsback]; sell short next bar on a limit at the close whenever close < close[barsback].

Plain English says 'if the current close is LESS than the close barsback ago, then enter a buy limit' (and greater for the short) — the opposite of the code. Also says the SHORT time is 300/2130 ('same times'), which the code does not. The code is authoritative (the ELD files run the code).

rules.name: No Exit Can Still Be An Exit
rules.rationale: Stop-and-reverse IS an exit: every entry that reverses closes the opposite position. Contrast the same entry gated to fire only when flat (which then has no exit at all). The two perform very differently.

rules.name: Start Simple
rules.rationale: Stop loss and profit target, four ways: fixed dollars; ATR-based; ATR-based with a dollar floor; ATR-based with a dollar ceiling. Author has many strategies with only a stop and no target, and some with neither.

Method 4: as 2 but each capped at stopdollarmax / profitdollarmax (MinList).

rules.name: Percentile Exit
rules.rationale: Exit when the close drops into the lower half of recent closes (for longs) or rises into the upper half (for shorts). Author used it in stocks and stock indices.

rules.rationale: After three consecutive closes in your favour the streak is likely to end (about 6% chance of a fourth), so take the profit. The consecutive closes may pre-date the entry, deliberately.

rules.name: Don't Give It All Back
rules.rationale: Let the position breathe but never give back more than a volatility-scaled amount of the peak open profit.

rules.rationale: Once a profit floor has been reached, keep a set percentage of the maximum open profit.
